clue.text: Brainless beauty cut weight

parts.note: brainless means dumb, stupid

indicators.note: cut says the word loses its tail letter

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A rude remark about a pretty but dim woman slimming down.
explanation.definitionFit: A short bar with weights at each end, lifted in exercise, is a kind of weight.

clue.text: Dismiss record within a specific measure

indicators.note: within puts the record inside the measure

parts.note: a dose is a specific measured amount of medicine
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Throwing out a record that fits within an exact measure.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove someone from office or power is to dismiss them.

clue.text: Fraternity, we hear, that one's sent for?

indicators.note: we hear says the brotherhood phrase is spoken, sounding like the catalogue-buying phrase

parts.note: a male order is a brotherhood, a society of men

explanation.surface: A fraternity one is summoned to join, by rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods ordered by post are things one sends for.

clue.text: Kill, as more masculine?

definitions.meaning: butch means masculine, so the comparative is more butch

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to slaughter, and also reads whimsically as the comparative of butch.

clue.text: Serious criminal kept in jail, if erroneously

indicators.note: kept in says the letters are held within the following words

explanation.surface: A serious criminal locked up in jail, perhaps wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner serving a life sentence has committed a grave offence.

clue.text: Second bag concealing one work of art

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: concealing means the pouch word hides the numeral inside it

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch in a body
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A second bag hiding a valuable artwork, like a smuggler's trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture made of small tiles or glass pieces is an artwork.

clue.text: Excessive employment ever so unlikely, university claimed

indicators.note: claimed means taken in, so the jumbled letters take the abbreviation inside
unlikely suggests the words come out in an improbable new arrangement

explanation.surface: A university accused of overworking staff, which seems unlikely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlikely' rearranges EVER SO into OVERSE, and 'claimed' takes in U.
explanation.definitionFit: Using something too much is excessive employment of it.

clue.text: A massage on a Caribbean island

indicators.note: on means placed next to, here before the final a in the down entry

parts.note: a rub is a massage

explanation.surface: A massage on a Caribbean holiday island.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch island off Venezuela lies in the Caribbean Sea.

clue.text: Capital in Antipodes under leadership of Britain — is fallible without it?

definitions.text: Capital in Antipodes under leadership of Britain — is fallible without it?

indicators.note: under in a down entry puts the letter below what comes before
without means outside, so the fallible phrase wraps around the letter

parts.note: can err means is fallible, capable of mistakes

indicators.note: leadership of takes the leading letter of Britain
capital in takes the capital, the first letter, of Antipodes

explanation.surface: A jibe that Australia's capital, once under British rule, would go astray without Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the capital of a country in the Antipodes that was once under British leadership.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of Australia, a country in the Antipodes.

clue.text: Wearer of glasses that's in possession of 'visibility', did you say?

indicators.note: did you say signals that the count of letters is spoken, sounding like the nickname

parts.note: the word visibility has four letter i's in it

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone has good visibility through their glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a teasing schoolyard nickname for someone in spectacles.

clue.text: Crucial moment as ace played?

parts.note: in tennis an ace is a serve the opponent cannot hit back, so the point is won with nothing coming over the net

explanation.surface: A tennis match turning on a single unreturnable serve.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase describes an ace: a point where no ball comes back.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the stage beyond which turning back is impossible, a decisive moment.

clue.text: Very different pacifier

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
other means different

explanation.definitionFit: Something that calms a baby or a person is a pacifier, a calming thing.

clue.text: Boy in libertine, some dish

indicators.note: in places the boy word inside the libertine word

parts.note: a roué is a debauched man, a libertine
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A young lad living with a rake sounds like quite a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some dish' looks like slang for an attractive person; it is the food.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled-up dish, such as a meat or sponge roll filled and rolled, is a culinary preparation.

clue.text: Raised ground always, one might suppose

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters of the preceding word are reworked

parts.note: ay (aye) is an archaic and Scots word for always

explanation.surface: A remark about raised land that stays put, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to concede a likely point, much like 'presumably' or 'I suppose'.

clue.text: Lashes welcomed by evil Italian

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken in by the evil word

parts.note: sin is evil, wrongdoing
cilia are eyelashes

explanation.surface: An evil Italian embracing punishment by lashes.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Sicily is a southern Italian.

clue.text: Tree that's more mature

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a common hedgerow tree and also means older, senior.

clue.text: Find somewhere to dance, surprisingly

parts.note: a disco is a club for dancing
very can mean to a surprising extent, as in very good

explanation.surface: Stumbling upon a place to dance, unexpectedly.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun sense: something come upon or found is a find.

clue.text: Funny city in Nevada carrying river northward

indicators.note: northward in a down entry means the result is read upward
carrying means the city word holds the river inside

parts.note: Reno is a city in Nevada
the Nile is an African river

explanation.surface: A funny scene of a Nevada city carrying a river north.
explanation.walkthrough: RENILENO read upward gives the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A short joke in a single line is a funny, a gag.

clue.text: Flat back squashing right cheek

indicators.note: squashing means the reversed word presses the letter into its middle
back says the level word is read in the other direction

parts.note: even means flat, level

explanation.surface: Someone with a flat back squashing their right cheek while sitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve and cheek both mean impudent boldness.

clue.text: A rebel of sorts seizing love, one embracing the stud?

indicators.note: seizing means the jumbled letters grab hold of the zero letter
of sorts suggests a version of the words, rearranged

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A rebel of sorts grabbing love and embracing a stallion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of sorts' rearranges A REBEL into EARLBE; 'seizing' takes in O. 'stud' suggests a horse, but it is an earring.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft fleshy base of the ear holds a pierced stud earring.

clue.text: Warm quality functions with sunshine, primarily

parts.note: cosines are trigonometric functions

indicators.note: primarily picks out the opening letter of sunshine

explanation.surface: A maths lesson where functions meet sunshine, of all things.
explanation.definitionFit: Snugness and comfortable warmth make up this pleasant quality.

clue.text: Item worn by women near item worn by men

parts.note: nigh means near
a tie is a neckwear item worn by men

explanation.surface: Clothing for women placed next to clothing for men.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is a garment worn by women in bed.

clue.text: Catalyst unknown in Yemen, sadly

indicators.note: in places the unknown inside the jumbled letters
sadly suggests the letters are in a sorry, disordered state

parts.note: Z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A sad report of a catalyst unknown in Yemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges YEMEN into ENYME, and Z goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A biological catalyst is a protein that speeds up a reaction.

clue.text: Generous smear enthralling artist

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the smear word holds the artist inside

parts.note: a libel is a smear, a written defamation
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A generous smear of paint captivating a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal means open-handed, giving freely.

clue.text: Stick sock on

parts.note: to sock is to hit, to bat

explanation.definitionFit: A short rod, as used by a conductor or relay runner, is a stick.

clue.text: Impede first of generals punching chap, private

indicators.note: punching means the letter drives into the chap word

parts.note: bod is slang for a person, a chap

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of generals

parts.note: own means private, personal, as in one's own room

explanation.surface: Generals punching a private soldier: army discipline gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' is not the soldier but the adjective for personal.
explanation.definitionFit: To get stuck or to hinder progress is to hamper movement, to impede.

clue.text: Something light, a chunk lifted

indicators.note: lifted in a down entry means the words are read upward

parts.note: a slab is a thick chunk

explanation.surface: A light piece of something, a chunk raised up.
explanation.definitionFit: This very lightweight wood is famously light, used in models.

clue.text: Game with very little chance of winning or not at all, one I try foolishly

definitions.text: Game with very little chance of winning

indicators.note: foolishly suggests the words are jumbled about without sense

parts.words: not at all, one I try

explanation.surface: A wry view of a gamble so hopeless one tries it only out of folly.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK's state lottery is a game where the odds of a jackpot are tiny.

clue.text: Bell for match

definitions.meaning: something that rings, like a bell

explanation.definitionFit: The word means one that rings, and a person so alike another they are a match.

clue.text: Bird never heard in novel

indicators.note: heard says the words are spoken, giving something that sounds like the title

parts.note: a jay is a bird of the crow family; ne'er is the old poetic form of never

explanation.surface: A bird that never makes itself heard in a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte Brontë's 1847 work is a famous English novel.
